title: 2nd Mystery The Ease Of Essential Power

questions.question: How is Allah’s power described at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: It is described as pure, exalted, radiant, and eternal, above all other lights.

questions.question: What is said about the inner reality of created things in relation to that power?
questions.answer: Their inner realities are presented as bright and reflective, like mirrors receiving what is shown to them.

questions.question: Which kinds of created things are mentioned to show the wide range of Allah’s command?
questions.answer: The passage mentions everything from tiny particles, plants, and animals to stars, suns, and moons.

questions.question: Why does the passage say creating countless things is as easy as creating one thing?
questions.answer: Because all things are fully under Allah’s command, and His power is not burdened or limited by number, size, or type.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about whether one divine act delays or blocks another?
questions.answer: It teaches that no task clashes with another, so one act does not slow down or prevent another.

questions.question: What main idea is shown by saying that large and small, many and few, particular and universal are all the same for that power?
questions.answer: It shows that Allah’s power is unrestricted and works equally easily on every level of creation.

questions.question: What example is used to show how order and obedience allow a huge thing to be moved easily?
questions.answer: The passage uses the image of a very large ship being moved as easily as a child pushes a toy.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the example of a commander sending either one soldier or a whole army with one order?
questions.answer: A single command can direct both a small number and a great number when those receiving the order are obedient.

questions.question: In the balance example, what does the walnut show?
questions.answer: It shows that under a precise law of balance, a very small addition can move even something extremely large.

questions.question: According to the passage, what stands behind the order, regularity, and balance seen in creation?
questions.answer: Divine justice and endless wisdom within Allah’s power stand behind them.

questions.question: How does the passage compare moving stars with moving atoms?
questions.answer: It says both are equally easy for Allah through the wisdom and order of His power.

questions.question: How does the passage compare giving life to one fly with giving life to an entire species and many living beings?
questions.answer: It says Allah gives life to one fly and to entire groups of living things with the same ease and command.

questions.question: What comparison is made between reviving a tree in spring and reviving the earth?
questions.answer: The passage says that giving life to a tree and bringing the whole earth back to life in spring are both done with ease.

questions.question: What does the phrase about hundreds of thousands of kinds of resurrection in spring mean?
questions.answer: It means spring displays many living renewals that resemble resurrection on a vast scale.

questions.question: What overall conclusion about Allah’s power should a reader take from this passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s power is perfectly ordered, wise, just, and unlimited, so nothing is hard for Him whether it is one thing or countless things.

questions.question: What central claim does the passage make about Allah’s power and the creation of many things?
questions.answer: It claims that creating endless things together is as easy for Allah as creating a single thing.

questions.question: What qualities of Allah’s power help explain this ease?
questions.answer: The passage points to its eternity, purity, radiance, and its connection with perfect wisdom and justice.

questions.question: How are created things presented as responding to Allah’s command?
questions.answer: They are shown as fully compliant and ready to follow His command.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention both atoms and heavenly bodies?
questions.answer: To show that Allah’s power reaches the smallest and the greatest without any difference in difficulty.

questions.question: What does the statement that no task interferes with another tell us about divine action?
questions.answer: It tells us that Allah’s actions are not limited the way human efforts are.

questions.question: In the example of the huge ship and the child’s toy, what is being compared?
questions.answer: The ease of moving something enormous is compared with the ease of moving something small when proper order is in place.

questions.question: What idea about authority is illustrated by the commander’s order to one soldier or to an army?
questions.answer: True authority can direct many as simply as it directs one when the command is effective and obeyed.

questions.question: How does the balance example support the passage’s main point?
questions.answer: It shows that a small cause can produce a major effect when a system is governed by precise law and equilibrium.

questions.question: What does the passage say is the source of all order and balance in creation?
questions.answer: It says they come from Divine justice and endless wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage connect wisdom and obedience to the movement of stars and atoms?
questions.answer: It teaches that both move under the same wise ordering power and obedient submission.

questions.question: What seasonal example is used to make the idea of resurrection easier to understand?
questions.answer: The revival of life in spring is used as a clear example.

questions.question: How does the passage use the example of flies to explain mass creation?
questions.answer: It says bringing one fly to life and bringing whole swarms and many species to life happen with equal ease for Allah.

questions.question: What does the phrase “plain of life” suggest in this passage?
questions.answer: It suggests the world of living existence into which creatures are sent forth.

questions.question: What inference can be made from the comparison between reviving a tree and reviving the earth?
questions.answer: If Allah easily revives one living thing, then reviving the earth on a vast scale is also easy for Him.

questions.question: What is the best summary of the passage in one sentence?
questions.answer: The passage teaches that because all creation is under Allah’s wise and just command, the greatest and smallest acts are equally easy for His power.

questions.question: According to the passage, what relationship exists between Allah’s power and light?
questions.answer: Allah’s power is presented as the highest and purest form of light.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the condition of things before Allah’s command?
questions.answer: It describes them as receptive and responsive, like polished surfaces ready to reflect.

questions.question: What does the passage emphasize by listing things from atoms to moons?
questions.answer: It emphasizes the complete range of creation under Allah’s authority.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about difference in scale before Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Differences in scale do not create differences in difficulty for Him.

questions.question: What human limitation is denied when the passage says one concern does not interfere with another?
questions.answer: It denies the limitation of being distracted, overburdened, or forced to choose between tasks.

questions.question: What principle is illustrated by the image of a large ship moved as easily as a toy?
questions.answer: Ordered power can direct something huge with ease when it is fully under control.

questions.question: Why is the military example effective in this passage?
questions.answer: It clearly shows that one command can govern either a single unit or a great number if obedience is present.

questions.question: In the scale example, why is the walnut important even though it is tiny?
questions.answer: It shows that size does not determine effect when a system works according to exact balance.

questions.question: What two divine qualities are directly linked to order and equilibrium?
questions.answer: Divine justice and endless wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the response of created things to Allah’s power?
questions.answer: They are described as obeying it and yielding to its operation.

questions.question: What comparison is made between stars and atoms?
questions.answer: Their movement is equally easy for Allah to direct.

questions.question: How does the passage use spring as evidence for its argument?
questions.answer: Spring shows a vast return of life, which points to Allah’s ability to revive creation on a larger scale.

questions.question: What does the passage say about bringing a single fly to life compared with whole classes of living things?
questions.answer: It says both happen by the same command and with the same ease.

questions.question: What does the mention of “hundreds of thousands” add to the description of spring?
questions.answer: It stresses the enormous variety and number of living forms revived at that time.

questions.question: What faith lesson does this passage aim to strengthen?
questions.answer: It strengthens trust that Allah’s power is unlimited, perfectly ordered, and fully capable of resurrection.

questions.question: What is the first reason the passage gives for why many things can be created as easily as one?
questions.answer: Allah’s power is exalted and radiant, and created things are fully under that power.

questions.question: How are the essences of things portrayed in relation to divine power?
questions.answer: They are portrayed as receptive and shining, able to display the effects of that power.

questions.question: What does the obedience of all created things imply about Allah’s rule over the universe?
questions.answer: It implies total rule and complete control over every part of creation.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw from that obedience?
questions.answer: It concludes that creating countless things side by side is entirely easy for Allah.

questions.question: Why is it important that no task interferes with another?
questions.answer: It shows that Allah’s power does not weaken or split when dealing with many matters at once.

questions.question: What does the image of the ship teach about the power of order?
questions.answer: Order can make the movement of something enormous simple and direct.

questions.question: What does the commander example teach about command and response?
questions.answer: When command is real and obedience is complete, one order can direct either one individual or a whole group.

questions.question: What is the main point of the two mountains on the balance?
questions.answer: Even immense masses can be moved through a subtle law of equilibrium.

questions.question: In this passage, what is said to be the beginning and foundation of order in creation?
questions.answer: Divine justice and unending wisdom within Allah’s power.

questions.question: How does the passage connect universal things and particular things?
questions.answer: It says both kinds are equally subject to Allah’s command and operation.

questions.question: What does the passage say Allah does with stars?
questions.answer: He causes them to move and revolve through the wisdom of His ordering.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the giving of life in spring?
questions.answer: It describes it as happening by a single command with ease, whether for one creature or many kinds.

questions.question: What comparison is made between a tree and the earth in spring?
questions.answer: Reviving a tree is compared to reviving the earth, and both are said to happen with ease.

questions.question: How does the passage help the reader understand resurrection?
questions.answer: It points to the yearly revival of life in spring as a smaller example of a greater rising.

questions.question: What is the overall message about divine power, wisdom, and justice?
questions.answer: They work together perfectly, making every act of creation and revival easy for Allah.

questions.question: What view of Allah’s power opens the passage?
questions.answer: It opens with the view that Allah’s power is the highest, purest, and most refined light.

questions.question: How does the passage describe all things from the smallest to the largest?
questions.answer: It describes them as obedient to Allah’s command and under His power.

questions.question: What does this obedience make “entirely natural,” according to the passage?
questions.answer: It makes it natural that countless things can be created together just as easily as one thing.

questions.question: What statement in the passage rejects the idea that Allah could be overwhelmed by many tasks?
questions.answer: The passage says that no task or concern interrupts another.

questions.question: Which pairs are used to show that Allah’s power treats all levels of creation equally?
questions.answer: The passage mentions great and small, many and few, and particular and universal.

questions.question: What is learned from the example of the giant ship?
questions.answer: Size does not make movement difficult when wise order and control are present.

questions.question: What is learned from the example of the commander and the army?
questions.answer: A single command can effectively direct one or many.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention a sensitive balance with mountains on it?
questions.answer: To show that through exact balance, even huge things can be affected as easily as smaller ones.

questions.question: What divine qualities are named as the source of cosmic order?
questions.answer: Absolute justice and endless wisdom are named.

questions.question: How are stars and atoms treated in the argument?
questions.answer: They are treated as equally easy for Allah to move.

questions.question: What does the fly example add to the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that giving life to one creature and to entire groups of creatures involves the same ease for Allah.

questions.question: What role does spring play in the reasoning of the passage?
questions.answer: It serves as visible proof that mass revival and renewal happen regularly by Allah’s command.

questions.question: What does the expression about the earth’s “corpse” suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that the earth in its lifeless state is revived again with new life in spring.

questions.question: What does the phrase about many examples of resurrection in spring mean?
questions.answer: It means spring contains many signs that resemble a bringing back to life after death.

questions.question: How might this passage strengthen a believer’s confidence in the Hereafter?
questions.answer: It shows that the One who revives the earth and all kinds of life with ease can also bring creation back again.

questions.question: What picture does the passage give of Allah’s power before giving any examples?
questions.answer: It presents Allah’s power as eternal, radiant, and supreme, with all creation under it.

questions.question: How are the realities of created things described so that the reader can understand their relation to divine power?
questions.answer: They are described as bright and mirror-like, able to receive and display what Allah wills.

questions.question: What broad sweep of creation is included in the passage’s examples?
questions.answer: It includes tiny particles, living things, and massive heavenly bodies.

questions.question: What major claim is made about one thing and many things in relation to Allah’s power?
questions.answer: There is no difference in difficulty between creating one thing and creating countless things.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying that one task does not interfere with another?
questions.answer: Allah’s power handles all matters together without delay, conflict, or weakness.

questions.question: How does the image of a child and a toy help explain a difficult idea?
questions.answer: It makes the idea simple by showing that what seems huge can be moved easily under proper control.

questions.question: What does the commander example show about the effect of a single command?
questions.answer: One command can send either one person or a whole army into action.

questions.question: How does the balance example deepen the argument beyond the commander example?
questions.answer: It adds the idea that exact order and measured balance allow even enormous things to shift through a very small cause.

questions.question: What does the passage identify as the root of all order and equilibrium in creation?
questions.answer: It identifies Divine justice and endless wisdom within Allah’s power.

questions.question: How does the passage use the movement of stars and atoms to support its teaching?
questions.answer: It says both move by the same divine ordering, proving that scale does not challenge Allah’s power.

questions.question: What does the mention of one fly and an entire species teach about life-giving power?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah gives life to individuals and entire groups with equal ease.

questions.question: How does the passage connect spring to the idea of resurrection?
questions.answer: Spring is shown as a repeated mass revival that points to the possibility and ease of resurrection.

questions.question: What does it mean that Allah revives the earth and also brings forth countless forms similar to the revival of a tree?
questions.answer: It means the same power that renews one living form also renews the whole earth in vast variety.

questions.question: What kind of reasoning does the passage mainly use to persuade the reader?
questions.answer: It uses examples from nature, order, command, and visible renewal to support belief in Allah’s unlimited power.

questions.question: What is the strongest concluding insight a student should take from this passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s power is so perfect in wisdom, justice, and command that the largest acts of creation and resurrection are as easy for Him as the smallest.
